clue.text: Admitting chatter during film is damaging for celebrities

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the damaging word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: mars means is damaging, spoils

indicators.note: during places the chatter within the film's title

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone gossiping through a screening is a nuisance for the famous people present.
explanation.walkthrough: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film; 'film is damaging' reads as one phrase but splits after 'film'.
explanation.definitionFit: Megastars are hugely famous performers, the biggest kind of celebrity.

clue.text: Bird's coat: stop short in wonder

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat

indicators.note: stop short means the word for wonder loses its last letter

parts.note: awe is wonder

explanation.surface: A bird's plumage makes you halt in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

clue.text: Not just a trombone slide

parts.note: a slide from note to note that any instrument, not only the trombone with its slide, can play

explanation.surface: A remark about the sliding part of a trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a series of notes in music.

clue.text: Where official heads for, when he's called over?

definitions.text: Where official heads for, when he's called over?

parts.words: Where official heads for, when he's called over?
parts.note: in cricket, after each over is called, the umpire moves to a fielding position level with the batsman

explanation.surface: A referee summoned across to deal with something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the umpire at the striker's end stands at SQUARE LEG, a fielding position square of the batsman; an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is the position the umpire walks to at the end of an over.

clue.text: Perhaps Victorian runs sport

parts.note: someone from the state of Victoria is an example of an Australian
rules means runs, governs

explanation.surface: A person from the Victorian era jogging for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests Queen Victoria's era, but it means someone from the Australian state of Victoria, the heartland of this football code.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian rules is a football code played mainly in Australia.

clue.text: Refuse to move seating to home stadium

parts.note: a stand is the seating area at a sports ground
a team's own ground is its home stadium

explanation.surface: A team declining to shift its stand to its home stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand one's ground is an idiom for holding firm and refusing to retreat.

clue.text: Jib, say, having to include son in heart of family

indicators.note: to include means the sail spar takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: a jib boom is a spar, so a jib is an example of a boom

explanation.surface: A sailing image: a jib taking a son aboard in the middle of family life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here; the definition is a phrase like 'in the bosom of the family'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom of a family is its warm, intimate centre, its heart.

clue.text: Fight and shout to overcome resistance

indicators.note: to overcome means the shouting word goes over and around the resistance letter

parts.note: bawl means shout
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fighting and shouting to beat opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy, rough fight.

clue.text: Formal argument succeeded for leader

indicators.note: for leader means the succeeded letter goes at the front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a tiff is a petty argument

explanation.surface: In a formal dispute someone succeeded in becoming leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are stilted and formal.

clue.text: City's awful, half buried in cash

indicators.note: buried in means the half word goes inside the cash

parts.note: money is cash

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word for awful is kept

parts.note: terrible means awful

explanation.surface: A city is a dreadful place, half of it smothered in money.
explanation.walkthrough: The cut synonym is the first half of an eight-letter word for awful, which the clue does not print.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterrey is a large industrial city in north-east Mexico.

clue.text: Sets of cryptic statements cracked by brainpower

indicators.note: cracked by means the statements are broken open with something inside them

parts.note: clues are cryptic statements, as in this puzzle
IQ, intelligence quotient, measures brainpower

explanation.surface: Crossword clues are solved by intelligence, a fair description of the solver's task.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliques are exclusive groups of people, close-knit sets.

clue.text: Darley, for one, had such telling nights

explanation.surface: A man named Darley spent nights telling stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Darley Arabian was one of the three founding stallions of the thoroughbred horse; the Arabian Nights are the tales Scheherazade told night after night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Darley Arabian is a famous horse of that breed, and the Arabian Nights are the storytelling nights.

clue.text: More sensible if husband abandons desire to meet queen

indicators.note: abandons means the husband's letter leaves the word for desire

parts.note: a wish is a desire
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: Advice that it would be smarter to give up longing in order to meet a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiser is the comparative of wise, so it means having more good sense.

clue.text: Read novel about lovers' leap hers?

definitions.text: Read novel about lovers' leap hers?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the lovers' leap
novel means new or unusual, so the letters of read are made anew

parts.note: a lovers' leap is a cliff from which lovers are said to have jumped

explanation.surface: An invitation to read a romantic novel with a lovers' leap in it, written by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Radcliffe wrote Gothic novels full of cliffs and peril, so the whole clue describes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann Radcliffe was the eighteenth-century Gothic novelist whose books feature dramatic cliffs and threatened heroines.

clue.text: A wet cut?

parts.note: a cut that is wet: a man-made channel dug and filled with water, rather than a hairdresser's wet cut

explanation.surface: A hairdresser offering to cut your hair while it is damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Canals were historically called cuts, artificial waterways dug through land.

clue.text: Hardback subdeacon translated

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church subdeacon's text turned into another language and bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the nine letters of SUBDEACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A case-bound book has stiff board covers, a hardback.

clue.text: A rose-red city — it bombed

explanation.surface: A city of roses that was attacked from the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is the emblem of Lancashire and its county town; the Avro Lancaster was the famous British Second World War bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The city takes the red rose as its emblem, and the four-engined RAF bomber of that name dropped bombs.

clue.text: Highlight, a banal red, needs redoing

indicators.note: needs redoing means the letters are done again in a new order

explanation.surface: A boring red paint highlight that the decorator must repaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs redoing' rearranges A BANAL RED. Aldebaran is the bright red star in Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, a highlight of it.

clue.text: Like chap's drink to be taken outside — it's wet

indicators.note: the drink goes outside, round the rest

parts.note: tea is a drink
as means like
man's is a chap's

explanation.surface: A man's drink should be carried outdoors because it is wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken outside' puts TEA round ASMANS. The Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea is a body of water, so wet in the extreme.

clue.text: A club member puts on back lawn

indicators.note: back means the word for puts on is read in reverse

parts.note: dons means puts on, as clothing
grass is a lawn

explanation.surface: A golfer or gardener laying turf on the back lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DONS into SNOD. Augustus Snodgrass is a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Snodgrass is one of the members of Mr Pickwick's club in Dickens's novel, a literary allusion.

clue.text: Study in this unclean state?

indicators.note: a messy state suggests the letters of study are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A remark about a study room that has been left grimy and neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: STUDY rearranged is a study covered in dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty means covered with dust, an unclean condition typical of a neglected study.

clue.text: One making no sense of book: afterwards, woman's got into it

indicators.note: got into means the woman's word sits inside the word for afterwards

parts.note: later means afterwards
her refers to a woman; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A tale about a book that a woman later got hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherer talks nonsense at length, someone who makes no sense.

clue.text: Weapon broadly distinguishing old convict

explanation.surface: A weapon that marked out a prisoner of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: British convicts' uniforms were marked with a broad arrow, a government mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a missile weapon, and the broad arrow was the mark printed on old convict clothing.

clue.text: Be indecisive? Hard to say with conviction

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Someone who is undecided finds it difficult to speak confidently.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver, a Scots and northern word, means to dither or hesitate.

clue.text: I broke nail in ornamental border

indicators.note: broke means the I breaks into the nail word, splitting it

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they broke a nail on a decorative edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Braid is woven trimming sewn on as decorative edging.

clue.text: Beau dressed in red and yellow

indicators.note: dressed in means the answer is clothed by the surrounding words

explanation.surface: A suitor wearing red and yellow clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau and a dandy are both men devoted to fashionable dress.

clue.text: Make sense of a French composer

parts.note: un is the French for a
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A reference to a particular French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a mystery is to work it out, to make sense of it.

clue.text: In revolt, international body brings in force

indicators.note: brings in means the international body contains the force word

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is an international body
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: During a rebellion the United Nations sends in troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisen means having risen up, as rebels in a revolt have.

clue.text: Sort of house wife embraced by active type

indicators.note: embraced by means the wife letter is hugged inside the active type

parts.note: a doer is an active person

explanation.surface: A wife being hugged by an energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dower house is the smaller home on an estate for the widow, so dower describes that kind of house.

clue.text: Still working, but not exercising one's talents?

definitions.text: Still working, but not exercising one's talents?

parts.words: Still working, but not exercising one's talents?
parts.note: someone working while staying still, using the seat rather than the body, as in a desk job

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a job that wastes their abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary job is done sitting still, with no physical exercise.
